title: Entropy Quantification Through Degree-Based Indices of Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Nanoribbon
content: Chemical graph theory applies mathematical graph-theoretical descriptors to characterize and quantify the features of molecular structures. Among the carbon nanostructures, Graphene nanoribbons have attracted considerable attention from researchers due to their distinctive structural and functional properties. Inspired by recent developments, this study investigates nitrogen-doped graphene nanoribbons NGR((n,m)).A molecular graph representation of the nitrogen-doped graphene nanoribbon is constructed, and its structural characteristics are analyzed through vertex and edge partition techniques. Based on these partitions, several degree-based topological descriptors, including the Zagreb indices, Forgotten index, Randic index, atom-bond connectivity index, geometric-arithmetic index, Harmonic index, and Sombor index, are derived in closed form. Furthermore, Shannon-type entropy indices computed from the descriptors quantify the nanoribbon’s degree of structural complexity and information density. This work provides a mathematical characterization of the topological structure of graphene nanoribbons, serving as a precursor to subsequent QSPR investigations. This proposed methodology extends graph-theoretical analysis to nitrogen-doped graphene nanoribbons and enables deeper exploration of molecular complexity using topological indices and entropy-based descriptors.
